findings.who: A filer whose brokerage or joint account in their name holds only stock or funds. Part of the ordinary dividends (or interest) belongs to a parent or child, so the filer received it as a nominee.
findings.why_no: The parent gate asks only about bonds or notes owned directly, savings bonds cashed, or interest on a loan or a property sold. A nominee holding stock answers no to each one truthfully, and the child question's 'any other adjustment to the interest or dividends' is never reached.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p.1: 'You received interest or ordinary dividends as a nominee'; p.2: 'enter "Nominee Distribution" ... Subtract this amount from the subtotal'
findings.fix: Add a separate gate, not nested under bonds: 'Did you or your spouse receive any interest or dividends in your name that actually belong to someone else (as a nominee)?' Alternatively, ask the special-treatment question whenever interest or dividends are above zero.

findings.who: A filer who holds brokered CDs, Treasury bills, or REMIC or other mortgage-backed regular interests that were bought on the secondary market at a premium or with acquisition premium. The Form 1099-INT shows box 11, or the Form 1099-OID shows box 6 or 10.
findings.why_no: None of these is called a 'bond or note' by the filer or the broker ('I own CDs and T-bills, not bonds'). The filer answers the gate no truthfully, and the question that names box 11, box 6 and box 10 never appears.
findings.irs_text: f1099oid p.7, Box 6: 'shows the amount of acquisition premium amortization for the year that reduces the amount of OID'; Box 10: 'shows the amount of premium amortization ... see the Instructions for Schedule B'
findings.fix: Gate on facts the filer can check: 'Does any Form 1099-INT show an amount in box 10, 11, 12 or 13, or any Form 1099-OID show an amount in box 6 or 10, or did you or your spouse buy any bond, note, CD, T-bill or other debt instrument (including in a brokerage account)?'

findings.who: A filer who owns corporate or Treasury bonds held in street name at a brokerage, bought at a premium or between interest dates.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'owned directly' as excluding bonds the broker holds for them, taking 'directly' to mean paper certificates or TreasuryDirect, as opposed to through a broker.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p.1: 'You are reporting interest income of less than the amount shown on a Form 1099 due to amortizable bond premium'; 'You have accrued interest from a bond'
findings.fix: Replace 'owned directly' with 'owned by you or your spouse, including in a brokerage account (not through a mutual fund or ETF)'.

findings.who: A filer who inherited, or bought, a promissory note secured by a home that someone else sold with seller financing. The buyer pays the filer interest on it.
findings.why_no: The filer neither made the loan nor sold the property, so 'interest on a loan made or a property sold' is a truthful no. The filer also does not think of a mortgage note as a 'bond or note owned'.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p.1: 'You received interest from a seller-financed mortgage and the buyer used the property as a personal residence'; 'Be sure to show the buyer's name, address, and SSN'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Did you or your spouse receive interest from an individual who owes you money on a mortgage, land contract or other loan, however you came to hold it?'

findings.who: A filer whose only interest is seller-financed mortgage interest paid by an individual buyer, who issues no Form 1099-INT.
findings.why_no: If 'taxable interest above zero' is computed from the forms the filer entered, the outer condition is false, and the seller-financing question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p.1: 'If you sold your home or other property and the buyer used the property as a personal residence, list first any interest the buyer paid you'
findings.fix: Compute the outer condition after an explicit question about interest received without a form, or ask about seller financing regardless of the interest total.

findings.who: A filer whose only interest is tax-exempt: municipal bonds or tax-exempt OID bonds bought at a premium, with Form 1099-INT box 13 or Form 1099-OID box 6, 10 or 11. Some also have market discount on a municipal bond that matured or was sold.
findings.why_no: Taxable interest, ordinary dividends and capital gain distributions are all zero, so the condition is false. The filer is never asked about the premium netting on line 2a, or about market discount, which is taxable interest even though no form shows it as taxable.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p.2: 'if you acquired a tax-exempt bond at a premium, only report the net amount of tax-exempt interest on line 2a'; p.1: 'The market discount on a tax-exempt bond is taxable interest income and not tax-exempt interest.'
findings.fix: Include tax-exempt interest and tax-exempt OID in the outer condition (interest of any kind above zero), or ask about bond premium and market discount whenever any 1099-INT or 1099-OID exists.

findings.who: On a joint return, the spouse alone holds premium bonds, cashed EE or I bonds for tuition, or carries a seller-financed mortgage.
findings.why_no: The gate is labeled 'Bonds or notes owned directly ... savings bonds cashed' with no 'you or your spouse', so the filer answering may report only their own holdings.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p.2, Line 3: 'you cashed series EE or I U.S. savings bonds issued after 1989 and you paid qualified higher education expenses for yourself, your spouse, or your dependents'
findings.fix: Word the gate as 'Did you or your spouse own bonds or notes, cash savings bonds, or receive interest on a loan or property sale?'

findings.who: A filer who sold a home with seller financing in 2019 and still receives interest from the buyer in 2025.
findings.why_no: The phrase 'a property sold' may be read as a sale this year.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p.1: 'You received interest from a seller-financed mortgage'
findings.fix: Add 'in any year' to the gate: 'interest received in 2025 on a loan you made or property you sold in any year'.

findings.who: A filer, or their spouse, owns more than 50% of a U.S. corporation, LLC or partnership. That entity holds a bank or brokerage account abroad, and the account is signed for by an employee or manager, not by the filer.
findings.why_no: Helper 1 asks whether "you (or ... your spouse) have an account in another country ... or the power to sign for one". The account belongs to the company, and the filer cannot sign on it. Helper 4 asks only about companies "set up outside the United States", and this company is domestic. Helper 2 asks about things "outside the United States", but the shares are in a U.S. company.
findings.irs_text: fincen114 p. 5, Financial Interest 2.b, "A corporation in which the United States person owns directly or indirectly: (i) more than 50 percent of the total value of shares"; c. (partnership); f. "Any other entity ... more than 50 percent"; i1040sb p. 3, "For definitions of 'financial interest' ... see the instructions for FinCEN Form 114."
findings.fix: Add to helper 1: "...or did a company or partnership that you (or your spouse) own more than half of, directly or through others, have such an account?"

findings.who: A filer is the beneficiary of more than half of the current income of a U.S. (domestic) trust, or is the grantor-owner of a domestic revocable living trust. The trust holds an account at a foreign bank or broker.
findings.why_no: Helper 3 covers only trusts that are "outside the United States, has a trustee abroad, or in which anyone other than a U.S. citizen ... can make or veto a decision", and this trust is domestic. Helper 1 asks whether "you" had the account, but the trust holds it.
findings.irs_text: fincen114 p. 5, Financial Interest 2.d, "A trust of which the United States person: (i) is the trust grantor and (ii) has an ownership interest"; 2.e, "A trust in which the United States person has a greater than 50 percent present beneficial interest in the assets or income of the trust"
findings.fix: Add to helper 1: "...or did a trust you set up and control, or whose current income goes mostly to you, hold such an account?"

findings.who: A filer has an account abroad that is held in the name of a relative, agent, lawyer or other nominee who manages it for the filer's benefit. A typical case is a parent overseas keeping the filer's savings in the parent's own name.
findings.why_no: Helper 1 asks whether "you ... have an account", and the account is in someone else's name. Helper 2's "owed money by someone abroad" does not read as covering one's own money that someone else holds.
findings.irs_text: fincen114 p. 5, Financial Interest 2.a, "An agent, nominee, attorney, or a person acting in some other capacity on behalf of the United States person with respect to the account"
findings.fix: Add to helper 1: "...including an account in someone else's name that is held for you".

findings.who: A filer holds a whole-life insurance policy or annuity with a cash value, issued by an insurer abroad, for example one bought before moving to the U.S. and still paid into.
findings.why_no: Helper 1 lists "a bank, investment, pension, payment or crypto account". A filer reads that list as complete, and an insurance policy is not on it. Helper 2's "anything else of value" seems to be about property, not a policy.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, "A financial account also includes ... an insurance policy with a cash value (such as a whole life insurance policy), an annuity policy with a cash value"; i8938 p. 7, "any cash value life insurance or annuity contract maintained by an insurance company or other foreign financial institution"
findings.fix: Add to helper 1's list: "an insurance policy or annuity with a cash value, or shares in a fund held directly with the fund".

findings.who: A filer living in the U.S. directly holds stock certificates or registered shares of a foreign corporation, a small interest in a foreign partnership or fund, a note from a foreign company, or a swap or option with a foreign counterparty. None of these is held through a financial account, and the documents are kept in the U.S.
findings.why_no: Helper 2 asks about owning anything of value "outside the United States". The filer reads that as where the asset physically is, and the certificate is in a U.S. drawer. Helper 4 applies only to a stake of "10% or more" or an officer role.
findings.irs_text: i8938 p. 7, "Stock issued by a foreign corporation. • A capital or profits interest in a foreign partnership. • A note, bond, debenture, or other form of indebtedness issued by a foreign person ... • ... similar agreement with a foreign counterparty"
findings.fix: Add a helper: "Did you (or your spouse) own, outside a U.S. brokerage or bank account, shares, bonds, notes, a partnership interest or a contract issued by or entered into with a foreign company or person, wherever the papers are kept?"

findings.who: A filer is the beneficiary of a foreign estate that is still being administered after a parent died abroad, and knows of the interest. Alternatively, the filer has an unvested deferred-compensation entitlement with a foreign employer that is not called a pension.
findings.why_no: Helper 3 names only a "trust or family foundation". Helper 2's "own" and "owed money" do not match an expected inheritance. Helper 1 names a "pension" account, but deferred pay is not called a pension.
findings.irs_text: i8938 p. 7, "An interest in a foreign trust or foreign estate"; p. 8, "Interests in Foreign Pension Plans and Foreign Deferred Compensation Plans ... Report in Part VI your interest"
findings.fix: Add "estate of someone who died" to helper 3, and "or deferred pay or bonus plan of an employer abroad" to helper 1.

findings.who: A parent elects Form 8814 to report a child's interest and dividends. The child holds foreign stock or a foreign account.
findings.why_no: Every helper asks about "you (or, on a joint return, your spouse)". The asset belongs to the child, so a truthful answer is no.
findings.irs_text: i8938 p. 8, "If you file Form 8814 ... you have an interest in any specified foreign financial asset held by the child."
findings.fix: When Form 8814 is in the return, ask the foreign-account and foreign-asset helpers about the child as well.

findings.who: A filer is a corporate treasurer or controller who approves wires or gives online or phone instructions on an employer's foreign account, alone or jointly with another person, but never signs anything.
findings.why_no: Helper 1 asks about "the power to sign for one". The filer reads "sign" literally and gives no signatures. The filer also takes the account to be the employer's, not theirs.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 3, "'Signature authority' is the authority of an individual (alone or in conjunction with another individual) to control the disposition of assets ... by direct communication (whether in writing or otherwise)"; "Don't consider the exceptions relating to signature authority in answering Question 1 on line 7a."
findings.fix: Replace "the power to sign for one" with "the authority, alone or with others, to move money from one (by signature, online, phone or otherwise), including an employer's or other person's account".

findings.who: A filer who owns 4% of a foreign corporation directly and is a partner in a U.S. partnership, or a beneficiary of a trust or estate, that owns another 8% of it. Or a filer who owns 6% and holds vested options or warrants for another 5%.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only whether they own 10% 'alone or with your family'. Shares held through partnerships, corporations, trusts or estates and shares they could buy through options are not 'alone' or 'with family', so a truthful no closes the gate. The gated question's help, which adds those shares, is never shown.
findings.line: sb.form5471_if_foreign (missed refusal; Form 5471 may be required)
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Part II TIP: 'You may also have to file Form 5471 if, in 2025, you owned 10% or more of the total (a) value of a foreign corporation's stock, or (b) combined voting power of all classes of a foreign corporation's stock with voting rights.'
findings.fix: Make the gate helper match the gated question: 'own 10% or more of its value or votes, counting shares of your spouse, children, grandchildren and parents, shares held by partnerships, corporations, trusts or estates you have an interest in, and shares any of you could buy through options or warrants.'

findings.who: A filer who in 2025 was an officer, director or manager of a corporation organized in Puerto Rico, Guam or the U.S. Virgin Islands but owned none of it, for example an executive of a PR subsidiary of their employer.
findings.why_no: Helper 1 says 'set up outside the United States', and they treat Puerto Rico and Guam as part of the United States (the FBAR definition says the same). Helper 2 asks whether they 'have ... a company' in a territory, which they read as owning one. They answer no to both. The gated question treats a territory company as foreign.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Part II TIP: 'You may have to file Form 5471 if, in 2025, you were an officer or director of a foreign corporation.'
findings.fix: In helper 1, say 'organized outside the 50 states and the District of Columbia (a company in Puerto Rico, Guam or another U.S. territory counts)'. In helper 2, add 'or were an officer, director or manager of a company there'.

findings.who: A filer who holds a class of voting shares carrying 10% or more of a foreign corporation's votes but under 10% of its value, or the reverse.
findings.why_no: 'An owner ... of 10% or more of one' reads as 10% of the company's equity or value. A filer measuring by value with under 10% answers no while holding 10% of the votes.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Part II TIP: '10% or more of the total (a) value of a foreign corporation's stock, or (b) combined voting power of all classes of a foreign corporation's stock with voting rights.'
findings.fix: Say '10% or more of its value or of its votes'.

findings.who: A U.S. employee named as a director or managing director of a foreign subsidiary of their U.S. employer, as a corporate formality with no ownership or pay from it.
findings.why_no: They do not think of the subsidiary as a company they have a role in for their own taxes. To them it is their employer's company, and the gate gives no example of a nominal or employer-assigned directorship.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Part II TIP: 'You may have to file Form 5471 if, in 2025, you were an officer or director of a foreign corporation.'
findings.fix: Add to the gate help: 'Count a title you hold at your employer's foreign subsidiary, even if unpaid or nominal.'

findings.who: A filer who set up, funds, or benefits from a trust that has only U.S. trustees and only U.S. decision-makers and is run day to day in a U.S. state. Its instrument names a foreign court or foreign governing law, or has a flight clause that moves the trust abroad if a U.S. court acts, so no court in the 50 states or D.C. has primary supervision.
findings.why_no: The gate asks only about a trust 'that is outside the United States, has a trustee abroad, or in which anyone other than a U.S. citizen, U.S. resident or U.S. company can make or veto a decision.' This trust is administered in the U.S. by U.S. trustees with no foreign decision-maker, so each clause is truthfully no. The gate never states the court test, which the line 8 help does explain.
findings.irs_text: cfr-26-301-7701-7 p. 1-2: 'A trust is a United States person if— (i) A court within the United States is able to exercise primary supervision over the administration of the trust (court test)'; the safe harbor requires that '(iii) The trust is not subject to an automatic migration provision'; 'The term foreign trust means any trust other than a domestic trust.'
findings.fix: Add to the gate: 'or a trust whose governing documents name a court or law outside the 50 states and D.C., direct that it be run outside the U.S., or move it abroad on some event (if you are not sure, answer Yes).' Better, state the court test and the control test in the gate's help, as the line 8 help already does.

findings.who: A filer, or the filer's spouse, who created a foreign trust or transferred assets to one years ago (for example in 2012). The trust still existed in 2025, but the filer had no dealings with it during 2025.
findings.why_no: The gate reads 'have, or did you have at any time in 2025, anything to do with a trust ... as the person who set it up, gave, sold or lent anything to it.' Many filers will take 'in 2025' to apply to the setting up or giving, and answer no because nothing happened that year.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 3, Line 8: 'If you were the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust that existed during 2025, you may have to file Form 3520'; i3520 p. 1, item 2: 'Note: You are required to complete Part II even if there have been no transactions involving the trust during the tax year.'
findings.fix: Reword the gate as 'Have you (or your spouse) ever set up, or at any time given, sold or lent anything to, such a trust that still existed at any time in 2025, whether or not anything happened in 2025?'

findings.who: A filer who stayed rent-free in a family villa or apartment abroad that a relative's foreign trust owns, or who borrowed from such a trust. It also covers a filer whose bank loan or credit card is guaranteed or secured by the trust's assets, or whose card charges the trust pays.
findings.why_no: The gate's 'received or may receive anything from it in any way' does not mention loans, free use of property or guarantees. Filers see a borrowed sum, a bank loan or a family holiday home as not 'receiving' anything from a trust, and may not see themselves as having 'anything to do with' it. Unlike the line 8 question, the gate shows no examples.
findings.irs_text: i3520 p. 4: 'used any property owned by a foreign trust without paying FMV within a reasonable amount of time, the amount of such loan or the FMV of the use of trust property will be treated as a distribution'; 'a loan by an unrelated third party that is guaranteed by a foreign trust is generally treated as a loan from the trust'; 'if charges you make on a credit card are paid by a foreign trust or guaranteed or secured by the assets of a foreign trust, the amount charged will be treated as a distribution.'
findings.fix: List these in the gate itself: 'including a loan from it, a loan or credit card it guarantees or secures or pays, or free or below-market use of a home, car or other property it owns, even if a relative arranged it.'

findings.who: A U.S. lawyer, consultant or seller who was paid by a foreign trust for services or property worth less than the payment, for example $100 for services worth $20. The filer is not a beneficiary.
findings.why_no: The filer sees the payment as a fee or a sale price, not as 'receiving anything' from the trust. The filer is not a family member, grantor or beneficiary, so 'anything to do with a trust or family foundation' reads as not applying to an arm's-length business dealing.
findings.irs_text: i3520 p. 4, Distribution: 'if you receive a payment from a foreign trust in exchange for property transferred to the trust or services rendered to the trust, and the FMV of the payment you received exceeds the FMV of the property transferred or services rendered, the excess will be treated as a distribution to you'; 'without regard to whether the recipient is designated as a beneficiary.'
findings.fix: Add to the gate: 'including payments for work or property you provided to such a trust, even as an outside professional or buyer.'

findings.who: A filer who received gifts, money or paid expenses from a foreign relative or an intermediary, where the money actually came from a foreign trust. A second case is a filer who is a partner or shareholder of a company that gave property to a foreign trust without a business purpose.
findings.why_no: The filer knows only of a gift from a person or of the company's act, and not of any trust, so 'anything to do with a trust or family foundation' is answered no. The phrase 'directly or through another person or company' is attached to giving, not to receiving, and filers do not see a company's transfer as their own.
findings.irs_text: i3520 p. 1, item 3: 'received, directly or indirectly, a distribution from a foreign trust'; i3520 p. 5, Grantor: 'If a partnership or corporation makes a gratuitous transfer to a trust, the partners or shareholders are generally treated as the grantors of the trust'; i3520 p. 6, Reportable Event: 'The transfer of any money or property, directly or indirectly, to a foreign trust by a U.S. person.'
findings.fix: Add 'including money or property that reached you through a relative, another person or a company, and transfers to such a trust by a company or partnership you own part of; if you are not sure where a gift came from, answer Yes.'

findings.who: A filer, or the filer's spouse, who holds a foreign tax-favored savings or pension arrangement set up legally as a trust that the filer can draw on, such as a Canadian TFSA or an individual foreign pension trust that is not exempt. Such an arrangement can make the filer the owner of a foreign grantor trust.
findings.why_no: The filer thinks of it as a savings or retirement account, not a 'trust or family foundation,' and may already have reported it as a foreign account elsewhere. The gate's wording suggests family estate planning.
findings.irs_text: i3520 p. 1, item 2: 'is treated as the owner of any part of the assets of a foreign trust under the rules of sections 671 through 679'; i3520 p. 5: 'A grantor trust is any trust to the extent that the assets of the trust are treated as owned by a person other than the trust'; i8938 p. 8: 'Interests in Foreign Pension Plans and Foreign Deferred Compensation Plans.'
findings.fix: Add to the gate: 'This includes a foreign savings, pension, education or investment plan set up as a trust (for example a Canadian TFSA or RESP), even if you think of it as an account; if you are not sure, answer Yes.'

findings.who: A filer whose only Form 1099-INT or 1099-DIV is issued under their SSN for an account whose income belongs to another person. Examples: a custodial or convenience account for a parent, or a joint account with a sibling. The filer has no other interest or dividends.
findings.why_no: The helper asks for 'Taxable interest' (and ordinary dividends). None of this income is taxable to the filer, so they enter $0 despite the words 'before any Schedule B adjustment'. The gate is then computed false.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1, Nominees: "If you received a Form 1099-INT that includes interest you received as a nominee ... report the total on line 1. Do this even if you later distributed some or all of this income to others." The p. 2 rule for dividends on line 5 is parallel.
findings.fix: Build the helper from the amounts shown on the forms: 'Total interest shown on every Form 1099-INT, 1099-OID or substitute statement issued in your (or your spouse's) name, even if it belongs to someone else.' Alternatively, ask sb.nominee whenever any 1099-INT, 1099-OID or 1099-DIV was received.

findings.who: A filer who sold a house or land with seller financing, possibly in an earlier year. They received 2025 interest from an individual buyer who issues no Form 1099-INT. The same applies to a filer who received interest on a private loan to a relative. Neither has any bank or brokerage interest.
findings.why_no: The phrase 'Taxable interest from all payers' reads as the total of the 1099 forms received. With no 1099, the filer enters $0. This prevents the question that names 'interest on a property you sold'.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1, Seller-financed mortgages: "If you sold your home or other property and the buyer used the property as a personal residence, list first any interest the buyer paid you ... Be sure to show the buyer's name, address, and SSN."
findings.fix: State in the interest helper that it includes interest with no form, such as interest from a buyer of property you sold (in any year) or on money you lent. Alternatively, ask sb.bonds_any regardless of the computed gate.

findings.who: A filer who holds only zero-coupon or other OID bonds or brokered CDs and receives only Form 1099-OID. They have no Form 1099-INT and no dividends.
findings.why_no: OID is not perceived as 'interest' because no interest was paid in cash and the form is not a 1099-INT. The filer enters $0 taxable interest.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1, Line 1: "Taxable interest generally should be shown on your Forms 1099-INT, Forms 1099-OID, or substitute statements." i1040sb p. 2, OID: "If you are reporting OID in an amount less than the amount shown in box 1 or box 8 of Form 1099-OID ... identify the amount to be subtracted as 'OID Adjustment.'"
findings.fix: Word the helper as 'Taxable interest, including original issue discount (Form 1099-OID box 1 or 8) and interest on Treasury or savings bonds'.

findings.who: A filer who holds only municipal bonds and bought one at a market discount, so accrued market discount is includible in 2025. Alternatively, a filer who cashed EE or I bonds to pay tuition and believes the interest is tax-free. Neither has other interest or dividends.
findings.why_no: The filer regards the muni income or the education-bond interest as tax-exempt. They enter $0 taxable interest, so the gate is false and the bond question is never reached.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 1: "The market discount on a tax-exempt bond is taxable interest income and not tax-exempt interest." i1040sb p. 1, Line 1: "Include interest from series EE, H, HH, and I U.S. savings bonds." p. 2, Line 3 covers the exclusion (Form 8815), which is claimed only after the interest is reported.
findings.fix: Add to the helper: 'Include savings bond interest even if you will exclude it for education, and market discount on a tax-exempt bond.' Alternatively, also trigger the gate when tax-exempt interest is above zero or when savings bonds were cashed.

findings.who: A filer whose 1099-INT interest is fully offset by an accrued-interest, OID or bond-premium adjustment. The filer enters the net amount in the interest helper, which comes to $0.
findings.why_no: The filer enters the amount they think is taxable after adjustments, not the gross figure on the form. The computed gate is then false.
findings.irs_text: i1040sb p. 2, Accrued interest: "If you received a Form 1099 for interest as a purchaser of a bond with accrued interest, follow the rules earlier under Nominees ... identify the amount to be subtracted as 'Accrued Interest.'"
findings.fix: Ask for the gross box amounts per form, and compute any net figure after sb.bonds_any is asked.
